summary: An early 1974 listing of information about ARPANET protocols, with pointers to documents and contacts. It is an old version of a document that was later revised; see RFC 694 for the update.

plainLanguage.summary: This file is a directory of ARPANET protocol work in November 1974. It points readers to documents and contacts, and marks entries described as official standards.

subtitle: Jon Postel's November 1974 directory of ARPANET protocols, documents and contacts.

tldr.problem: Information about ARPANET protocols, their documents and the people responsible for them needed to be gathered in one place.
tldr.mechanism: The file groups protocol activity by network level and lists contacts, documents, people, schedules and recent developments, marking official standards.
tldr.outcome: It is a dated snapshot of protocol activity in November 1974. The unit metadata says RFC 694 updates it.

today: The unit metadata says RFC 661 is updated by RFC 694. This file is a historical snapshot of protocol activity in November 1974, not a current directory.

sections.title: Purpose and Organization
sections.content:
RFC 661 is a file of information about protocols in the ARPA Network. Jon Postel says he will try to keep it current, but depends on readers to send information about developments and corrections.

It compiles protocol-related activity, much of it experimental. The label [Official] marks protocols that are official standards. When a document is online, the file provides a pointer to it.
sections.plainLanguage: The file gathers information about network protocols in one directory. It marks some as official and points to documents for more detail.

sections.title: Protocol Groups and Directory Entries
sections.content:
The directory groups entries under IMP-IMP, IMP-HOST, HOST-HOST, HOST-FRONTEND and PROCESS-PROCESS, followed by programs and National Software Works. Entries use headings for contact, documents, people, schedule and recent developments, although some headings have no information.

The listed subjects include the IMP-Host interface, NCP, TCP, Network Voice Protocol, Telnet, FTP, mail, remote job entry, graphics and other work. Online RFCs are noted as available through Office-1 in the <NETINFO> directory using names of the form RFCnnn.TXT.
sections.plainLanguage: The directory sorts protocol work by the computers or processes involved. Each entry points to people and documents and may describe recent changes.

sections.title: Examples of Developments Recorded
sections.content:
For the IMP-Host interface, the file notes that the link number field was extended from 8 to 12 bits and renamed the message identification field. It also says message type 6 indicates a reason for a type 7 destination-dead message, and points to RFC 660 for important interface changes.

The TCP entry records ongoing specification work and an addressing field described as 4-bit format, 4-bit network, 16-bit TCP and 24-bit process and port. The Telnet entry notes new implementations, a server socket, and newly defined options for controlling carriage return, line feed, form feed, horizontal tab and vertical tab behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: The directory captures changes in progress, including a wider interface field and new Telnet options. These notes describe the state of work at the time, not a timeless protocol guide.

sections.title: The National Software Works
sections.content:
The final major entry describes the National Software Works (NSW), which was developing protocols for its use of the ARPA Network. Its Procedure Call Protocol was intended to support sharing resources at the subroutine level and to divide NLS into front-end and back-end components.

The RFC describes a Version 2 set of documents, says it differs substantially from Version 1, and lists what each document covers. The directory says a demonstration of the NSW concept was planned for July 1975.
sections.plainLanguage: The directory also describes a set of documents for software that would let programs share remote procedures and data. It records the planned demonstration date as a future event at the time.

references.text: Walden, D., "Some Changes to the IMP and the IMP/HOST Interface", RFC 660, 23-Oct-74.
